vectors.name: exclude_overlapping_squares
vectors._derivation: XOR of [0,10]^2 and [5,15]^2 is the two L-shapes left after removing the [5,10]^2 overlap: each of area 100-25 = 75, total 150. They meet only at the isolated points (10,5) and (5,10), so the derived-correct representation is TWO simple rings, which is what ring_count pins.
vectors._known_gap: BOTH active ports currently emit ONE self-touching ring of twelve vertices that visits (10,5) and (5,10) twice, so ring_count is 1, not 2. The region (area and sample points) is correct; the ring violates the simple-ring assumption every PolygonSet consumer makes. Root cause: connect_edges walks the result boundary edge by edge and at a pinch vertex cannot tell which of the two touching regions it is on, so it walks into one lobe, out, and on into the other. The fix is a split-at-repeated-vertex post-pass on connect_edges output (prototyped, exact and region-preserving: cutting at the repeat gives loops of 75 + 75). It is BLOCKED on a separate port divergence it exposes: a multi-ring boolean result is materialised as ONE even-odd Path in jas_dioxus (controller.rs apply_destructive_boolean) but as N INDEPENDENT Polygon elements in JasSwift (Controller.swift applyDestructiveBoolean), and Swift Path has no fillRule field at all, so parity needs an element-schema addition. Landing the split before that would break the boolean_exclude_overlapping_rects action golden differently in each port. Hence ring_count ALONE is held out of the golden-oracle pass (via _known_gap_keys; area and sample_points stay gated, since they are correct today) in scripts/cross_language_algorithms.py (by this very `_known_gap` key); every other boolean and boolean_normalize vector is gated against its pinned expectation. Closing the gap means deleting this key. The port divergence and the unblock recipe are recorded in transcripts/BOOLEAN.md, under Multi-ring results: a live port divergence.
